items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Bachelor's Degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Masters Degree in Education, Counseling, Social Work or a related field.
Demonstrated experience implementing initiatives that enhance equitable outcomes for historically minoritized students in higher education.
Experience with grant-funded programs, including implementation, reporting, and compliance.
Experience designing and implementing programs that support student access, enrollment, transition, and early academic success.
Experience working with programs that support first-generation, low-income, or transfer student populations.
Multicultural humility; knowledge and experience working and interacting effectively with staff, faculty and student populations from a broad range of perspectives, backgrounds and experiences.

Demonstrated experience developing and leading access, outreach, and/or transition initiatives in higher education, including work with K–12 schools, community colleges, and/or community-based organizations.

Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Associate Director will provide leadership and oversight of partnerships and projects that promote equitable outcomes and experiences for students who are underrepresented, low income, first generation college students, and/or otherwise at a higher risk of experiencing academic difficulty. The Associate Director will work collaboratively with regional community colleges, SAPEP high schools, regional counties of education, Educational Partnership Center (EPC), Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) Initiatives, the Office of Black Student Success, the Educational Opportunities Program, and the Office of Admissions to establish student-centered guided pathways and redress policy and practices that create institutional barriers for prospective and newly admitted students.
Familiarity with statewide or systemwide college access initiatives (e.g., intersegmental partnerships, outreach programs, or transfer pathway programs).
Advanced knowledge of trends, issues, and state / federal policies in higher education policies, and practices related to college access, first-year transition, and transfer pathways.
Bilingual or multilingual communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex situations, exercise sound judgment, and develop effective, solutions-oriented strategies.
Excellent written, verbal, and digital communication skills, with the ability to engage with audiences of broad perspectives and backgrounds.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments, divisions, and external partners.
Demonstrated ability to supervise, train, and develop professional staff, including setting goals, managing performance, and fostering a collaborative team environment.
Demonstrated ability to use data and assessment tools to evaluate program effectiveness and inform continuous improvement.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to plan, implement, and assess multiple initiatives simultaneously.
Demonstrated ability to build and sustain partnerships across educational systems (K–12, community colleges, and universities) and with community stakeholders.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
